title: Ordinary integral cup product on arbitrary abelian etale sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use abelian sheaves on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Put $A=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z)$ in the common coefficient universe. Use the exact scalar-forgetting functor $U_X$ and its canonical inverse-image comparison [def-sbc-raw-module-scalar-pullback-comparison]. This is an equivalence for $A=\mathbf Z$; write $L_X$ for its inverse and $\epsilon_F:U_X L_X F\simeq F$ for its counit. Define $F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G=U_X(L_XF\otimes_A L_XG)$, with the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and define its maps by $U_X(L_Xa\otimes L_Xb)$. The canonical inverse-image tensor comparison is the module inverse-image tensorator, conjugated by the scalar-forgetting comparison and these counits; denote it by $q_{f,F,G}:f^{-1}(F\otimes G)\to f^{-1}F\otimes f^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Use the integral-generator class comparison $\kappa_M^n:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X,A)}(A_X,M[n])\to H^n(X,U_XM)$ of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class] and ordinary cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. This comparison is bijective for integral coefficients. For $e:F\otimes G\to H$, $p,q\geq0$, $x\in H^p(X,F)$, $y\in H^q(X,G)$, lift the classes through $H(\epsilon^{-1})$ and $\kappa^{-1}$ to derived morphisms $\widetilde x:A_X\to L_XF[p]$, $\widetilde y:A_X\to L_XG[q]$. Define $x\smile_e y$ by transporting back through $\kappa$ and $H(\epsilon_H)$ the composite $A_X\to A_X\otimes^L A_X\xrightarrow{\widetilde x\otimes^L\widetilde y}(L_XF\otimes^L L_XG)[p+q]\to(L_XF\otimes L_XG)[p+q]\xrightarrow{\widetilde e[p+q]}L_XH[p+q]$, using [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Here the first arrow is the inverse unit constraint, the shifts are moved out of the right factor first and then the left factor (the unsigned cocycle convention), the penultimate arrow is the localization lax tensorator followed by the canonical tensor-of-single-complexes identification, and $\widetilde e$ is the unique module arrow with $U_X(\widetilde e)=e\circ\epsilon_H^{-1}$. This is the ordinary derived-global-sections cup, expressed by the derived adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf Z,R\Gamma(-)[n])=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf Z_X,-[n])$.
